name: Self-sealing brain implant coating
subtitle: insulation that reseals so brain implants last decades

effects.effect: capsules in a plastic burst when it cracks and glue the crack shut

effect: capsules in a plastic burst when it cracks and glue the crack shut
how: Brain implants that let paralysed people type or move a robot arm usually fail within a few years, as body fluid seeps through hairline cracks in the insulation and corrodes the wires. A coating seeded with tiny capsules bursts when it cracks and fills the gap with fresh insulation, so the implant could keep listening to neurons for decades.
obstacle: The healing agent has to be safe in the brain, and the capsules small enough not to thicken hair-thin electrodes.
why: Implant lifetime is the field's biggest problem; no self-healing coating has been implanted.
real: Self-healing encapsulants (e.g. a water-resistant self-healing fluoroelastomer for implanted antennas) exist at materials level; none shown on neural implants in vivo.
